feature.title: The debate: buy the Nvidia pop, or fade it?
body: **The case for buying.** The report cleared the biggest event risk in tech. Revenue was $115.8 billion against about $109 billion expected, and the $130 billion guide sits far above the Street. After a slide that took Nvidia down roughly a quarter or more from its record, positioning is light, so good news forces covering. Buyers point to the rest of the AI complex moving with it as proof the cycle is intact.

**The case for fading.** Overnight gaps often fade by the close. The $130 billion guide includes an extra week, gross margin is guided down to about 71% to 72%, and the Fed's minutes at 2:00 PM ET could revive the 50bp debate and push yields up. Sellers say a gap up after a big drawdown is a chance to cut, not to add.

**How to say it in an interview.** 'I'd wait: the headline is strong, but the quality of the guide and the Fed minutes decide whether the gap holds. I'd buy a hold into the afternoon and sell a failure.' Pick the camp you believe and be ready to say what would change your mind.

stories.headline: Nvidia revenue jumps 103% to $115.8 billion and it guides to $130 billion in its first report since Huang left
stories.dek: Revenue beat Nvidia's own $108 billion guide and the Street's $109 billion, but the outlook includes an extra week and gross margin is set to fall to about 71% to 72%.
stories.updateNote: Rewritten with the actual results, the $130 billion outlook and margin commentary.
tldr: Third-quarter revenue was **$115.8 billion**, up 103% from a year earlier, with Data Center at **$107.6 billion** and non-GAAP EPS of **$2.68**, per Nvidia's release.
Fourth-quarter guidance is **$130.0 billion, plus or minus 3%**, and includes an additional week; it assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China.
Kress said gross margin should bottom around **71% to 72%** in the fourth quarter as memory and component costs rise. One report had the stock up more than 2% after hours.
whatHappened: Nvidia reported fiscal third-quarter results after the close on Tuesday. Revenue was $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier and well above the $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, that the company guided to in August (a range topping out near $110 billion) and the roughly $109 billion [[consensus]] expected. Data Center revenue was $107.6 billion, non-GAAP diluted earnings per share were $2.68, and GAAP [[gross margin]] was 74.8%, per the company's release.

The outlook was the bigger event. Nvidia's fourth-quarter [[guidance]] is $130.0 billion, plus or minus 3%, and the company says the figure includes an additional week. It assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China. Colette Kress, the CFO who is also interim CEO, said memory prices and component costs will pressure margins, with fourth-quarter gross margin at roughly 71% to 72%, down from about 74% in the third quarter, in line with her August message that margins would bottom in the fourth quarter.

This was the first report since Jensen Huang resigned. One report had the stock up more than 2% in after-hours trading; I could not confirm a settled move, and Tuesday's regular-session close was not available.
background: Nvidia reported in the middle of a drawdown: the stock had fallen sharply from its record on the CEO exit, a short-seller report and a three-day slide in the Nasdaq. A report that beats the guide by this much resets the question from 'is the AI trade cracking?' to 'what is the quality of the growth?'

Two details matter for that question. The extra week in the outlook flatters the sequential jump to $130 billion without a change in demand. And falling gross margin means each dollar of sales earns less, even as revenue grows.
whyItMatters: A big beat and a raised outlook from the AI bellwether is the strongest single argument against the three-day selloff, and it lands before the Fed minutes and APEC. The reaction on Wednesday morning will show whether the market buys the growth or focuses on margins and the extra week. Watch [[implied volatility]]: if it drops sharply, the event risk has been cleared.

grandLine.title: A Coup de Burst, not a new engine
grandLine.body: The Thousand Sunny burns barrels of cola for a huge emergency jump. It is powerful and costly, and it cannot be done all the time. A guide that includes an additional week is a bit like that: it gets the number a long way forward in one leap, but it does not mean the ship's engine got stronger. The test is what the next ordinary quarter looks like.

views.camp: Beat and raise, AI trade intact
views.argument: Revenue topped the guide by a wide margin, Data Center is the engine at $107.6 billion, and the outlook is far above the Street. With positioning light after the selloff, a clean report can restart the rally.

views.thesis: The headline overstates the underlying acceleration.
views.argument: The $130 billion outlook includes an extra week, gross margin is set to fall to about 71% to 72%, and China adds nothing. A rally that leans on the headline can fade once those details sink in.

interview.question: Nvidia beat by a wide margin and guided to $130 billion, but margins are falling. Is it a buy?
interview.answer: The quarter was strong, but I'd focus on the quality of the guide. The $130 billion includes an additional week, so the sequential jump overstates demand, and gross margin is set to fall to about 71% to 72%. I'd want to see how the stock holds after the first reaction before adding. What would change my mind is a margin outlook that slips below that range or a sign that hyperscaler orders are slowing, which would hit the multiple.

followUp.question: Why does gross margin matter if revenue is up 103%?
followUp.answer: Because the market pays for profit, not sales. If margin falls, each extra dollar of revenue earns less, so profit grows slower than revenue, and the stock's multiple can compress even on a beat.

trade.expression: Long a one-month at-the-money call, short a call about 10% out of the money (call spread)
trade.rationale: If the beat-and-raise holds and positioning stays light after the drawdown, the stock can retrace part of the drop. Selling the upper call finances part of the premium after implied volatility falls.
risks: The extra week and margin decline fade the rally, so the premium is lost.
A weak Nasdaq tape or a hot Fed minutes release can overwhelm a single-stock beat.

keyTerms.definition: The average analyst forecast for a company's results; beating it is the baseline for a positive reaction.
keyTerms.example: About $109 billion of revenue for Nvidia this quarter.

keyTerms.definition: A company's own forecast of its future results. Markets often react more to the guide for the next quarter than to the quarter just reported.
keyTerms.example: Nvidia's guide was about $108 billion, plus or minus 2%.

keyTerms.definition: Revenue minus the direct cost of the product, as a share of revenue. A falling gross margin means each sale earns less profit.
keyTerms.example: Kress said in August that gross margin would bottom in the fourth quarter.

keyTerms.definition: The market's expected size of future price swings, backed out of option prices. It rises when investors pay up for protection, then usually drops after the event.

stories.headline: Nasdaq falls 2.5% and the S&P 500 drops 1.9% as AI stocks slide into Nvidia's first report without Huang
stories.dek: The S&P 500 lost a third straight session, closing at 7,416.59, and the Dow fell 1.4%. Defensive sectors held up while chips and AI names led the selloff.
tldr: Technology led the damage, with Nvidia the focus a day before its first earnings report since Jensen Huang resigned; consumer staples and health care were the exceptions.
The Nasdaq's drop is bigger than all of last week's 2.3% gain, so the rebound that followed the Nasdaq's slide earlier this month is gone.
whatHappened: U.S. stocks sold off hard on Monday, with technology leading. The S&P 500 shed 145.08 points, or 1.92%, to 7,416.59, its third straight loss. The Nasdaq Composite fell 626.52 points, or 2.49%, to 24,509.76, and the Dow dropped 739.38 points, or 1.41%, to 51,608.17, per AP and CNBC closing reports. Those figures line up exactly with Friday's closes (7,561.67, 25,136.27 and 52,347.55). Reuters-based reports quoted smaller intraday declines at points during the session.

Reports pointed at chip and AI names and at Nvidia in particular. The stock was down roughly 4% in afternoon trading, according to one report, with investors reluctant to hold it into Tuesday's [[event risk]]: the first report under interim CEO Colette Kress. Rising bond yields were also cited as a weight. Consumer staples and health care were the exceptions, a classic [[risk-off]] pattern in which money moves toward defensive groups.
background: The Nasdaq has now handed back more than it gained last week, when it rose about 2.3%. That rebound followed the post-election correction, and it leaned on two things: falling oil and a cooler producer-price report. Both have faded. Nvidia, the biggest single weight in the Nasdaq, has also lost its CEO since then, so index moves track its stock more tightly than usual.
whyItMatters: When the largest AI stock is the swing factor, the next move depends on one report. A clean beat with steady guidance can unwind a lot of the fear quickly, because positioning is already lighter. A weak outlook would confirm the worry that the AI trade is cracking, and with the S&P 500 down three days in a row there is less cushion. Watch [[implied volatility]]: if option prices stay high after the report, the market is still braced for more.

grandLine.title: Aqua Laguna on Tuesday
grandLine.body: In Water 7 everyone knows the giant tidal wave Aqua Laguna is coming, and the city still has to evacuate to high ground. Monday looks like that evacuation: with Nvidia's report on a known date, many investors cut exposure before the wave rather than after new information arrived. That is why a scheduled event can drag prices down in the days before it.

views.thesis: This is positioning, not a verdict on AI.
views.argument: Nvidia's date is fixed and the CEO change adds uncertainty, so traders trimmed beforehand. If guidance holds, the selling reverses, because the fundamentals have not changed.

views.thesis: Three down sessions plus a CEO exit is a trend, not a blip.
views.argument: With yields rising and the AI leader leaderless, the easy money has been made. A merely in-line report may not be enough to restart the rally.

interview.question: The Nasdaq is down 2.5% the day before Nvidia reports. Do you buy it or wait?
interview.answer: I'd wait for the report. The move looks like pre-earnings de-risking, and the outcome is binary on guidance, so I'd rather not own the gap in either direction. If Kress holds the revenue guide and margins, I'd look to buy the dip in the leaders. What would change my mind is a cut to the outlook or a sign the board is reconsidering the plan, which would make me think the AI trade has broken rather than paused.

followUp.question: How would you express a view on the report without owning the stock?
followUp.answer: A put spread on the Nasdaq-100 caps the cost and the risk, while a straddle pays on a big move in either direction. Because option prices already reflect the event, I'd compare implied move against how far the stock has actually moved on past reports.

trade.expression: Long QQQ near-dated 5% out-of-the-money put, short a 10% out-of-the-money put (put spread)
trade.rationale: If Tuesday's report disappoints and the selloff extends, the spread pays off at a defined cost. Selling the lower put reduces the premium after a volatile day.
risks: A strong report or steady guidance sends the Nasdaq sharply higher and the premium is lost.
Implied volatility is already high, so the spread is more expensive than usual and a calm reaction erodes it.

keyTerms.definition: The chance that a known, scheduled event (earnings, a data release) moves a price sharply, so traders adjust positions before it.

keyTerms.definition: A market mood where investors sell volatile assets such as tech and buy defensive ones such as staples, health care and Treasuries.
keyTerms.example: Staples and health care rose Monday while tech fell.

keyTerms.definition: The market's expected size of future price swings, backed out of option prices. It rises when investors pay up for protection.
keyTerms.example: Option prices on Nvidia and the Nasdaq-100 are the gauge for Tuesday's expected move.

stories.headline: Fed minutes arrive Wednesday after Waller said a 50bp hike should be considered in December
stories.dek: Waller backs at least 25 basis points and sees room for more if inflation stays hot. Hammack and Williams speak this week, and Chair Warsh gives no guidance.
tldr: Governor Christopher Waller said on Nov. 10 he would support a 25bp hike in December and that a larger move may be needed if core prices rise 0.3% or more.
The minutes of the October meeting come out Wednesday at 2:00 PM ET; Hammack and Williams are among the Fed speakers this week, per a Newsquawk schedule.
whatHappened: In a speech in London on Nov. 10, Waller said he would back a 25 basis point increase at the December meeting even if October inflation improves, and that a 50 basis point hike should be considered if core prices rose 0.3% or more from September. Core CPI rose 0.3% in October. Reuters contrasted his guidance with Chair Kevin Warsh's resistance to giving any rate-path guidance.
A Newsquawk schedule lists Hammack speaking Tuesday and Williams on Wednesday, the same day the minutes of the October meeting are due.
whyItMatters: The minutes show how many officials were open to a larger move. A division would keep 50bp alive; a consensus for 25 would pull it back. Rates are the channel that moves Nvidia's multiple, which is why Wednesday matters for tech.

stories.headline: Anthropic is set to list on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT; the debut date and pricing are not confirmed
stories.dek: The AI company filed its S-1 on Oct. 26. One IPO calendar points to trading this week, but I could not confirm the date.
tldr: Anthropic filed a Form S-1 and applied to list Class A shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT.
One IPO calendar lists first trading for Nov. 19; I found no company confirmation, and the price range and size had not been set in the filing.
whatHappened: Anthropic filed its S-1 with the SEC on Oct. 26, saying it applied to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under ANT, per Decrypt and InvestingLive. The filing did not set a share count or price range. Reports put the target valuation near $2 trillion, which remains preliminary. ABC7 reports the company is set to make its market debut; one IPO calendar lists Nov. 19.
Disclosure: this paper is written by Claude, which Anthropic makes.
whyItMatters: A very large AI listing adds supply to a market that has just sold off in tech, and it competes for the same AI-focused money as Nvidia. Big IPOs also tend to mark the later part of a rally, so desks will watch pricing and the first-day move.

stories.headline: Futures jump as Nvidia's blowout quarter pulls AI and chip stocks higher after hours
stories.dek: Nasdaq 100 futures rose about 1.4% to 1.5% and S&P 500 futures about 0.7% after Nvidia beat estimates; the stock was up roughly 2% to 5% after the close.
tldr: Nasdaq 100 futures rose about **1.4% to 1.5%** and S&P 500 e-mini futures about **0.7%** after Nvidia's report, per Investing.com and other reports.
Nvidia closed Tuesday at **$155.46**, down 0.44%, then rose between about 2% and 5% after hours, depending on the report and the time.
Sympathy moves: CoreWeave about +5%, Micron about +4.4%, Nebius about +4% and AMD about +3.8% after hours; the Fed's minutes at 2:00 PM ET are the next test.
whatHappened: Nvidia reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion against about $109.15 billion expected, and adjusted earnings of $2.68 per share against $2.47 expected, with fourth-quarter guidance of $130.0 billion. Overnight, Nasdaq 100 [[futures]] were up about 1.4% to 1.5% and S&P 500 e-mini futures about 0.7%. Reports of Nvidia's after-hours gain ranged from about 2.3% to nearly 5%, depending on the time of day.

Related AI and chip names rose in a [[sympathy move]]: CoreWeave about 5%, Micron about 4.4%, Nebius about 4% and AMD about 3.8%, per Investing.com. The rebound follows a rough stretch: Nvidia slid into the print on Tuesday, and a CNBC live-blog headline reports that the Dow fell more than 800 points and the S&P 500 posted its lowest close since July; I could not confirm exact closing levels.
background: The AI trade was pricing in more bad news than the report delivered. Nvidia had fallen roughly a quarter or more from its record by different counts after the CEO exit and a short-seller report, so a beat with a higher guide forced shorts and hedgers to cover. That is how a stock can gap up on good news after a drop.
Overnight futures are an early guide, not a close. They have to survive the open and the Fed's minutes at 2:00 PM ET.
whyItMatters: The report took the biggest idiosyncratic risk off the table for tech, so the Nasdaq has room to retrace part of its three-day slide. The risk is that the rally is a short-covering [[positioning]] move that fades if the minutes read hawkish or if the margin story (about 71% to 72% in the fourth quarter) gets more attention than the headline beat.

grandLine.title: The Log Pose points to the next island
grandLine.body: A Log Pose only points to the next island after it has stayed on this one long enough to record it. Nvidia's report gave the market its reading for this island; the Fed's minutes at 2:00 PM ET are the next. Until the needle settles on that one, a futures jump is a heading, not a destination.

views.thesis: The biggest event risk cleared and positioning was light.
views.argument: With Nvidia beating by a wide margin and guiding well above the Street, shorts cover and the sidelined money returns. The Nasdaq's three-day slide gives it room to retrace.

views.thesis: Overnight gains often fade by the close.
views.argument: The guide includes an extra week, gross margin is set to fall, and the Fed's minutes could revive the 50bp debate. If yields rise again the multiple compresses, so a gap up can be a chance to sell.

interview.question: Nasdaq futures are up about 1.4% on Nvidia's beat. Do you chase it at the open?
interview.answer: I wouldn't chase the open. Overnight gains after a big drawdown are often positioning, and the Fed's minutes at 2:00 PM could change the rate story. I'd rather see how the market holds the gains through the morning and into the minutes. What would make me buy is a hold of the gap into the afternoon on strong breadth; what would make me sell is a rise in the 10-year yield that sends tech back down.

followUp.question: Why do chip stocks like Micron and AMD move with Nvidia?
followUp.answer: They sell into the same AI spending cycle, so one customer budget and one demand signal moves all of them. Nvidia's beat is read as proof the cycle is intact, which lifts the group in a sympathy move.

trade.idea: Long Nasdaq-100, short S&P 500 relative value
trade.expression: Long Nasdaq-100 futures, short S&P 500 e-mini futures, sized beta-neutral
trade.rationale: If the AI rebound continues, tech outperforms the broader index after being the weakest part of the market. The short S&P leg hedges overall market direction.
risks: A hawkish Fed minutes release hits long-duration tech harder than the index.
The gap fades and tech gives back its relative gain.

keyTerms.definition: Contracts that track an index's expected level; they trade nearly around the clock and are used as an early read before the stock market opens.
keyTerms.example: Nasdaq 100 futures were up about 1.4% to 1.5% overnight.

keyTerms.definition: When related stocks move in the same direction as a stock that just reported, because they depend on the same demand.
keyTerms.example: Micron and AMD rose with Nvidia.

keyTerms.definition: How investors are already invested; when many are short or hedged, good news can force buying and a sharp move.
keyTerms.example: Light positioning after the selloff made a short-covering rally possible.

watchNext.what: Whether the futures gains hold through the open.

stories.headline: Chip-export curbs are expected to dominate the Trump–Xi talks as APEC opens in Shenzhen
stories.dek: Both leaders have confirmed they will attend each other's APEC and G20 summits. The trade truce already runs to January 10, so the open question is chips.
tldr: APEC leaders meet in Shenzhen on Nov. 18–19; the G20 follows Dec. 14–15 in Miami, and both leaders confirmed intent to attend each other's summits.
Reuters reported that the prospect of tighter US limits on China's access to advanced AI chips is likely to dominate the talks, per Daily Sabah.
whatHappened: The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit opens in Shenzhen with a Trump–Xi meeting expected, their third this year. The US–China trade truce was already extended to January 10, so tariffs are not the headline. According to Reuters, as cited by Daily Sabah, the possibility of tighter US restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips is likely to dominate. I found no reporting yet on the talks themselves.
whyItMatters: Nvidia's fourth-quarter outlook already assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China, so a new curb mostly affects the sentiment around chip names rather than Nvidia's guide. A softer line on chips would be upside for semiconductors.
